note.p: Robert Ker Porter DNB 1777-1842 see the event tag of 2.5.1800 which refers to Godwin's attendance at the showing of Porter's hugely popular panorama of The Taking of Seringapatam in the fourth Mysore War. Porter was in Russia for several years and then fo a long period after 1815 Consul to Venezuela (but he was back in 1835). His brother, William Ogilvie Porter, seems to have lived largely in Bristol. It seems possible that the Porters in 1800 are references to this porter. The day after the exhibition Godwin sees a Porter at Bedford House (an 'adv'), and there is an 'adv' a few day before at a RA exhibition (and then a slightly odd entry at the Milton Gallery on May 17 1800, which may also be him). The additional oddity is that the express reference to R K Porter only occurs in July 1802, but this might be because the vast majority of his previous contacts have been 'adv' in character - and thus not a positive meeting with. But this makes it less probable that the Porter who appears on Godwin's travels later in May at Sheridan's is this Porter, and this has not been coded under this person.
